chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkill (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Jameel ibn Salih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),
regarding His saying, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'Our Lord, grant us in this world a good deed and in the Hereafter a good deed.'
He said: The satisfaction of Allah and Paradise are in the Hereafter, and sufficiency in sustenance, livelihood, and good character are in this world.

key_terms.حَسَنَةً: a good deed or good thing

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the 'good' of this world and the 'good' of the Hereafter according to Shia interpretation?
ai.summary: In Ma'ani al-Akhbar, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s (AS) practical exegesis of the Prophetic supplication, grounding the abstract concept of 'hasanah' in tangible worldly blessings like sustenance and character. This interpretation highlights the Shia emphasis on balancing spiritual aspiration with material well-being, viewing worldly provision not as a distraction but as a component of divine favor. By linking 'husn al-khuluq' (moral excellence) to the worldly good, the Imam underscores that ethical conduct is integral to the holistic 'good' sought in this life.
